newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Commerce economist sees Q1 GDP above 3.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Commerce economist sees Q1 GDP above 3.8 pct.

text.p: Commerce Department Chief Economist Lee Price said Friday that buoyant consumption could push Gross Domestic Product growth in the first quarter of the year past the vigorous 3.8 percent pace of the fourth quarter.
"It could well be stronger than the strong fourth quarter 3.8 (pct)," Price said in an interview on Reuters Financial Television.

Price, interviewed after the department reported a 0.2 percent gain in March retail sales and a sharp upwardly revised 1.5 percent jump in February sales, said the recent selloff in stock prices was unlikely to curtail consumption, since the previous run-up has not added much to consumption.
"We had very strong consumption demand," he said, adding that the rate of first quarter consumption in current dollars is close to double digits.
"I think consumption across the board shows a confident consumer," he added.
Besides consumption, Price saw strength in demand for building materials, construction activity and investment.
"So, our other parts of the economy beyond retail sales will give positive contributions as well," he said.
Despite the healthy consumption and broad-based economic strength, Price said inflation has been tame.
"I think inflation doesn't present a serious risk to the economy at this point," he said.
